The Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth , [ b ] [ c ] also referred to as Poland–Lithuania or the First Polish Republic ( Polish : I Rzeczpospolita ), [ d ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] was a federative real union [ 12 ] between the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania , existing from 1569 to 1795. This state was among the largest, [ 13 ] [ 14 ] most populated countries of 16th- to 18th-century Europe. At its peak in the early 17th century, the Commonwealth spanned approximately 1,000,000 km 2 (390,000 sq mi) [ 15 ] [ 16 ] and supported a multi-ethnic population of around 12 million as of 1618. [ 17 ] [ 18 ] The official languages of the Commonwealth were Polish and Latin , with Catholicism as the state religion .
